metadata.title: Gaia DR4 Wide Binaries: the Pre-Data Record of a Screened, Newtonian Prediction and Its Scoring Rule (Archive Note)
metadata.description:
Archive note, version 1.0 (2026-11-15), made before the Gaia DR4 release that ESA lists, provisionally, for 2 December 2026. No DR4 byte existed when it was made. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; not reproduced by any outside group. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed; nothing here says the data favour this framework.

This record is a time stamp, not a result. It puts in one archive everything this research programme registered for Gaia DR4 wide binaries before the data: the prediction of the theory the record currently adopts (wide binaries are screened and Newtonian; radial boost at most 4.45e-5 / 4.01e-5 at 30 kAU on the two footings), the rule that will score it (the fork rows of 2026-10-22 as fixed by the owner decisions of 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-15, with the R statistic beside them), the pre-registration of 2026-07-16 with its 22 amendments, and the release-day tools with their DR3 code-path checks.

The frozen pipeline cannot tell the adopted theory's prediction from Newton's. So DR4 can count against the theory, if the sky shows a boost, and it cannot confirm it: a Newtonian sky is survival, never confirmation. With the sample size forecast for DR4 (about 8,000 pairs) and a large systematic error, a Newtonian sky reads UNDECIDED.

The pre-registration and the decisions were public in the project's git repository from their own dates. As far as the record shows, this is their first deposit under a DOI; the date this DOI vouches for is 2026-11-15.

Files: the cover note (PDF) and one archive (zip) with a manifest of every file's sha256 and the repository commit. The archive holds DR3 code-path outputs and mock runs; none of them is evidence about gravity. The record's own scorecard of 2026-11-12 reads: no registered prediction has come true.
